questions.chapterTitle: Materials Handling, Powered Industrial Trucks, and Rigging
questions.stem: A forklift turns sharply while carrying a raised, off-center load. Which combined effect creates the greatest tip-over concern?
options: The elevated and shifted combined center of gravity can move outside the stability area under lateral acceleration
Turning force affects only the tires and cannot shift the stability relationship
The raised load lowers the center of gravity and increases the stability margin
An off-center load is safe whenever its total weight is below rated capacity
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Forklift stability depends on the combined center of gravity remaining within the stability area. Height, lateral offset, speed, and turning reduce the margin even below nominal capacity.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The option 'Turning force affects only the tires and cannot shift the stability relationship' does not apply the controlling principle for forklift stability triangle to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'The raised load lowers the center of gravity and increases the stability margin' does not apply the controlling principle for forklift stability triangle to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'An off-center load is safe whenever its total weight is below rated capacity' does not apply the controlling principle for forklift stability triangle to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: A truck is rated for 4,000 pounds at a 24-inch load center. A long load moves the actual load center substantially farther forward. What should the operator conclude?
options: Keep the 4,000-pound rating because the data plate is assumed not to change with load geometry
Available capacity is reduced, so the load must be evaluated using the truck data and any approved attachment or derating information
Move the mast forward and travel slowly, treating operating technique as sufficient compensation for the longer load center
Add locally selected counterweight and continue operating without manufacturer-approved capacity or data-plate information
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A longer load center increases overturning moment and can reduce capacity. Unauthorized counterweights or mast positioning do not restore the listed rating.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The option 'Keep the 4,000-pound rating because the data plate is assumed not to change with load geometry' does not apply the controlling principle for forklift load center and capacity to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Move the mast forward and travel slowly, treating operating technique as sufficient compensation for the longer load center' does not apply the controlling principle for forklift load center and capacity to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Add locally selected counterweight and continue operating without manufacturer-approved capacity or data-plate information' does not apply the controlling principle for forklift load center and capacity to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: A warehouse has frequent near misses where forklifts reverse through blind intersections used by pedestrians. Which control is strongest?
options: Remove near misses from the log because no one was struck
Issue high-visibility vests and leave routes and intersections unchanged
Redesign traffic flow to separate people and trucks, improve sight distance and controls, and verify speeds and right-of-way behavior
Tell pedestrians to listen for backup alarms as the sole control
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Physical separation and traffic-system design are more reliable than visibility apparel or alarms alone, especially at predictable conflict points.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The option 'Remove near misses from the log because no one was struck' does not apply the controlling principle for pedestrian and forklift separation to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Issue high-visibility vests and leave routes and intersections unchanged' does not apply the controlling principle for pedestrian and forklift separation to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Tell pedestrians to listen for backup alarms as the sole control' does not apply the controlling principle for pedestrian and forklift separation to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: A forklift must enter a detached trailer at a dock. What should be verified before entry?
options: That the driver remains in the cab with the engine running
Only the forklift’s fuel level because the trailer is not powered equipment
That the dockboard is the same color as the dock edge
Trailer restraint or wheel control, landing gear support as needed, dockboard capacity and securement, floor condition, lighting, and trailer stability
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Trailer movement, collapse, dockboard failure, poor flooring, and visibility can be catastrophic. A pre-entry system must address each interface.

The option 'Only the forklift’s fuel level because the trailer is not powered equipment' does not apply the controlling principle for trailer and dock safety to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.
The option 'That the dockboard is the same color as the dock edge' does not apply the controlling principle for trailer and dock safety to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: A synthetic web sling has a cut exposing load-bearing yarns. The lift is light and scheduled to last one minute. What is the correct decision?
options: Remove the sling from service under the applicable rejection criteria and use a suitable inspected replacement
Use it once because short lift duration offsets sling damage
Reduce the load by 10% and continue without manufacturer evaluation
Tie a knot over the cut to restore rated capacity
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Damage affecting load-bearing material is a removal condition. Duration and informal repairs do not establish capacity.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The option 'Use it once because short lift duration offsets sling damage' does not apply the controlling principle for sling inspection and removal to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Reduce the load by 10% and continue without manufacturer evaluation' does not apply the controlling principle for sling inspection and removal to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.
The option 'Tie a knot over the cut to restore rated capacity' does not apply the controlling principle for sling inspection and removal to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: A two-leg sling lifts a symmetric load. The sling legs are changed from near vertical to a much flatter angle while load weight stays the same. What happens to leg tension?
options: Leg tension decreases to zero as the legs approach horizontal
Leg tension increases as the sling angle becomes flatter
Only hook weight changes; sling angle has no force effect
Leg tension remains equal to half the load at every angle
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Flatter sling angles require greater horizontal and total leg forces to support the same vertical load, potentially exceeding component ratings.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The option 'Leg tension decreases to zero as the legs approach horizontal' does not apply the controlling principle for rigging angle forces to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Leg tension remains equal to half the load at every angle' does not apply the controlling principle for rigging angle forces to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: A supervisor directs employees to guide a load by standing beneath it because the tag line is too short. What should the lift director require?
options: Lower the load faster to reduce time under suspension
Allow the practice when workers wear hard hats
Stop the lift, keep personnel clear of the suspended load and fall zone, and provide an appropriate method to control the load
Use hand contact from directly below because it provides better control
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: People should not be positioned under suspended loads. Tag lines, planning, positioning, and other controls must manage the load without exposing workers to its fall path.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The option 'Lower the load faster to reduce time under suspension' does not apply the controlling principle for suspended load exclusion to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Use hand contact from directly below because it provides better control' does not apply the controlling principle for suspended load exclusion to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: A jam occurs inside a guarded conveyor transfer point. Operators routinely reach through an opening while the belt runs slowly. Which correction is most defensible?
options: Enlarge the opening so workers can reach more comfortably
Keep slow speed because low-speed conveyors cannot cause serious injury
Use a spotter while the conveyor remains energized
Eliminate routine reach-in, improve guarding or jam-clearing design, and isolate hazardous energy before access
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Slow movement can still entangle or crush. The design should prevent access and enable remote clearing or verified energy isolation.

questions.stem: At a dockboard assessment, a supervisor proposes: "An off-center load is safe whenever its total weight is below rated capacity". The underlying case is: A forklift turns sharply while carrying a raised, off-center load. Which combined effect creates the greatest tip-over concern? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: The raised load lowers the center of gravity and increases the stability margin
An off-center load is safe whenever its total weight is below rated capacity
The elevated and shifted combined center of gravity can move outside the stability area under lateral acceleration
Turning force affects only the tires and cannot shift the stability relationship
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Forklift stability depends on the combined center of gravity remaining within the stability area. Height, lateral offset, speed, and turning reduce the margin even below nominal capacity.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'The raised load lowers the center of gravity and increases the stability margin' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling forklift stability triangle principle.
The proposed response 'An off-center load is safe whenever its total weight is below rated capacity' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling forklift stability triangle principle.
The proposed response 'Turning force affects only the tires and cannot shift the stability relationship' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling forklift stability triangle principle.
